subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Editing and Evaluation Phases
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Editing and Evaluation Phases.

hook.text: Before choosing, your brain simplifies options: rounding numbers, ignoring small differences, setting a reference.

buildup.text: Prospect theory has two phases. First, editing: the brain organizes and simplifies the choice.

discovery.text: Second, evaluation: the edited options are compared using the value function and probability weights.

twist.text: The editing phase is where most biases enter. How you frame a problem determines how it gets evaluated.

climax.text: The same gamble, presented differently, gets different edits and different choices. Frame creates preference.

punchline.text: How you see the choice is the choice.

quiz.question: What happens in prospect theory's editing phase?
options: The brain simplifies and organizes options before evaluating
People skip directly to a final choice

details.summary: Prospect theory proposes that decisions happen in two phases: an editing phase where options are simplified and framed, and an evaluation phase where the simplified options are assessed using the value function and probability weighting.
details.whyItMatters: The editing phase is where framing effects enter decisions. How options are initially simplified determines what gets evaluated, meaning the presentation and context of choices shape outcomes before any calculation begins.
takeaways: Editing simplifies options through coding, combination, and segregation
The evaluation phase applies the S-shaped value function to edited prospects
Framing effects arise because editing changes how options are perceived

faq.question: What happens during the editing phase of a decision?
faq.answer: People simplify complex choices by rounding probabilities, combining similar outcomes, and setting a reference point. This mental shortcutting reduces cognitive load but introduces systematic biases into the evaluation that follows.

faq.question: Why does the editing phase matter for marketers?
faq.answer: Because the way options are initially framed determines how they are edited and evaluated. A price shown as a discount from a higher reference creates a different mental frame than the same price shown as a standalone number.
